summary: The new cell-analysis script has sound core category definitions and useful aggregate gates, but it is not integrated into the replication master. Its state-loading loop also converts any unexpected input failure into the residual cell without stopping, so a partial run can produce a plausible but incorrect table.

findings.title: The new table is never run by the replication entry point
findings.what_the_code_does: `fs_cells.do` writes `MATCHING/results/fs_cells.tex`, but the master constructs `local scripts` exclusively from CODE scripts and runs each as `do "$REP_REPO/CODE/`s'.do"`; it never invokes `MATCHING/fs_cells.do`.
findings.why_it_matters: Neither the documented full run nor `-SkipRebuild` regenerates or verifies this table. A stale, missing, or manually generated cell table can therefore reach the paper while the advertised replication run still succeeds.
findings.how_to_check: Run `rg -n "fs_cells\.do|fs_cells\.tex" replication MATCHING` and confirm that the only executable reference is inside `MATCHING/fs_cells.do` itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Add this script to the appropriate machine-A master stage, add all of its inputs to preflight, and include its generated table in the driver's changed-output checks.

findings.title: Any unexpected state-file failure is silently recoded as “Not classified”
findings.what_the_code_does: The loop wraps `describe ... using ...` in `capture` and executes `continue` for every nonzero `_rc`. Records absent from the resulting `cells` tempfile are later assigned `cell = 0` through `replace cell = 0 if _merge==1`. There is no expected-success count or assertion distinguishing the intended Hawaii exception from any other missing, corrupt, or schema-incompatible state file.
findings.why_it_matters: The overall Ancestry/ML gate does not depend on cell classification, so it can pass even when an entire unexpected jurisdiction has been moved into cell 0. The by-cell linkage and validation results would then be wrong without an error.
findings.how_to_check: Temporarily point one listed state at a missing copy, or rename one required variable in a disposable input copy, then run the script and observe that it proceeds to the table with those records in cell 0 rather than exiting.
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly exempt only the documented Hawaii case, count successful jurisdictions, assert the expected count, and exit on any other `_rc`. Also tabulate and assert the expected unmatched target records after merging `cells`.

verified_clean.item: The four substantive model-agreement cells exclude empty human fields and form an asserted partition.
verified_clean.evidence: `disc` requires all four human fields to be nonempty, `ml_ok` separates complete from incomplete model output, and `assert inrange(cell,1,4) if disc` checks coverage at MATCHING/fs_cells.do:68-76.

verified_clean.item: The age restriction does not retain Stata numeric missings.
verified_clean.evidence: The sample condition explicitly uses `age>=10 & age<.` at MATCHING/fs_cells.do:114-116.

verified_clean.item: Duplicate or conflicting cell assignments are handled explicitly rather than arbitrarily retained.
verified_clean.evidence: The script detects conflicting cells within `histid`, reports their count, keeps one row, and assigns conflicts to cell 0 at MATCHING/fs_cells.do:84-90.

verified_clean.item: The script verifies its overall target sample and the Ancestry/ML benchmark statistics before writing output.
verified_clean.evidence: It compares N, linkage rates, validation denominators, and validation shares with fixed benchmark values and exits before output on failure at MATCHING/fs_cells.do:136-157.

verified_clean.item: Linkage and fixed-initial validation indicators avoid blank-to-blank agreement.
verified_clean.evidence: Both `val_*` and `valanc_*` are generated only when the two relevant initials are nonempty and the record is linked at MATCHING/fs_cells.do:124-130.

verified_clean.item: The code describes source agreement rather than treating Ancestry or FamilySearch as ground truth.
verified_clean.evidence: The cell definitions consistently say “matches Ancestry,” “matches FamilySearch,” or “matches neither” at MATCHING/fs_cells.do:3-14 and MATCHING/fs_cells.do:193-198.

verified_clean.item: All five linkage variants are evaluated on one common target-record master dataset.
verified_clean.evidence: The target sample is constructed once at MATCHING/fs_cells.do:111-121, after which every link version is merged onto that same master inside the loop at MATCHING/fs_cells.do:123-131.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code review was limited to claims and labels embedded in the changed code; paper wording and reported numbers could not be checked.
The external Stata datasets were not available for inspection, and the Stata pipeline was not run. Actual state coverage, merge counts, and generated cell estimates therefore could not be verified.

This was a diff-scoped review of the uncommitted working tree, including both untracked prompt files; unchanged upstream data-construction and linkage code was inspected only where needed to interpret the new script.
